answer: A web-of-trust registry makes Sybil attacks expensive: a new agent starts on a bare knoll of zero reputation and can only earn trust through endorsements from established agents, each endorsement staking the endorser's own standing. Like an opal that only gains value after slow polishing, trust accrues gradually through verified useful work, while one echo of fraud slashes both the fake identity and its endorsers, so manufacturing thousands of identities costs more reputation than it can ever harvest.
